description: SIMONA is an agent-based simulation environment for large-scale electricity grid simulations with a focus on distribution grids. Its citation title describes it as a discrete-event distribution grid simulation environment, and it produces close-to-reality time series that can be used to analyse a given power grid, for example for distribution grid planning, flexibility analysis or studies of coupled sector interdependencies. The framework includes out-of-the-box models for many grid participants and their operational behaviour. It is developed at the Institute of Energy Systems, Energy Efficiency and Energy Economics (ie3) of TU Dortmund University and used in several research projects, so the codebase is continuously under development. It is location independent: any distribution grid described in the input data model can be simulated. The code is written in Scala, hosted on GitHub (latest version tag 4.0.0) with documentation on read-the-docs, under the BSD 3-Clause licence at no cost. Caveats: the README states that the codebase is continuously under development by different research projects and developers, so users should expect change, and it names no packaged release on a public registry. Simulation uses are agent-based simulation, network flow and distribution grid planning. Related records: it complements model-pandapower and model-pypsa, which use different network representations.
